test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 30 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
In the question below there are three statements followed by two conclusions I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the three statements disregarding commonly known facts.

Statements:

Only Car are Vehicle.

Some Car are Bulky.

All Metal are Bulky.

Conclusions:

I. Some Vehicle are not Metal.

II. Some Metal are Car.
solution:
Given Statements:

Only Car are Vehicle.

Some Car are Bulky.

All Metal are Bulky.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/12ad1e5100a706ade8bd6d5efcf3e0de40310b267a933e55960e326429ecc10a.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some Vehicle are not Metal – **True **

⇒ Vehicles are a part of Cars
⇒ Metals are a part of Bulky
⇒ There is no direct connection between Vehicle and Metal
⇒ Vehicles cannot be Metals (since only Cars are Vehicles)
⇒ So, some Vehicles are definitely not Metal

II. Some Metal are Car – False 
⇒ Some Cars are Bulky
⇒ But no definite overlap between Metal and Car is given
⇒ They may or may not intersect

Hence, only conclusion I follows.

The correct answer is **Option 3**.
